title: Detergents & Surfactants — DPP characteristics
description: Field specifications for the Detergents & Surfactants Digital Product Passport, shaped for UNTP's credentialSubject.characteristics extension point. Economic operators and facility identifiers are carried by the UNTP envelope and are deliberately absent here.

gtin.title: GTIN
gtin.description: Global Trade Item Number (GTIN-14) for the product.
gtin.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

batchLotNumber.title: Batch / Lot ID
batchLotNumber.description: Production batch or lot identifier for traceability.

packagingImageUrl.title: Packaging Image URL
packagingImageUrl.description: URL to a product packaging image for visual identification.

commodityCode.title: Commodity Code (TARIC)
commodityCode.description: TARIC combined nomenclature code for customs classification.
commodityCode.x-citationNote: Annex VI Part A(f) requires the commodity codes 'where applicable', so the field is optional; Reg (EEC) 2658/87 itself is a nomenclature, not a duty to publish a code.

productCategory.title: Product Category
productCategory.description: Main product category (e.g. detergent, paint, lubricant, adhesive).
productCategory.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. detergentUserType.title: Consumer or Industrial Use
detergentUserType.description: Whether the detergent is for consumers or is an industrial and institutional detergent (placed on the market for use only outside the domestic sphere, by specialised personnel; Reg (EU) 2026/405 Art. 2). The passport's full substance list (Annex VI Part A(h)) binds consumer detergents; an industrial and institutional one may rely on its safety data sheet instead.
detergentUserType.x-citationNote: The classifier the passport's Part A(h) exemption turns on. The label must indicate an industrial and institutional detergent (Annex V Part A 1(f)); the definition is in Art. 2.

productSubcategory.title: Product Subcategory
productSubcategory.description: Subcategory further specifying the product type.
productSubcategory.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

manufacturerPhone.title: Manufacturer Phone
manufacturerPhone.description: Contact telephone number for the manufacturer.

passportServiceProvider.title: Passport Service Provider
passportServiceProvider.description: Entity providing the DPP issuance service.

countryOfManufacture.title: Country of Manufacture
countryOfManufacture.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code where the product was manufactured.
countryOfManufacture.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

preservatives.title: Preservatives
preservatives.description: Array of preservatives with substance name and CAS number.
preservatives.x-citationNote: Preservatives reach consumers through the CLP label and, where applicable, sector labelling rules; CLP itself creates no separate duty to publish a preservative list as product data. Its labelling duty is discharged by what is affixed to the package.

fragranceAllergens.title: Fragrance Allergens
fragranceAllergens.description: Array of fragrance allergens present above threshold, with CAS numbers.
fragranceAllergens.x-citationNote: Fragrance allergen disclosure is a LABELLING duty in the sector instruments that impose it, not a CLP one — CLP's own obligation is the hazard label. Publishing the list here is useful to allergic users but is not how the duty is discharged.

hazardClass.title: Hazard Classes
hazardClass.description: Array of CLP/GHS hazard classifications applicable to the product.
hazardClass.x-citationNote: CLP Arts. 17-21 put the hazard information on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous. A labelling duty, not a passport one; empty for an unclassified mixture. Reg. (EU) 2026/405 Annex VI Part A carries no CLP item; Part B lets the passport include the Art. 17 label information.

signalWord.title: Signal Word
signalWord.x-citationNote: CLP Art. 20: the signal word ('Danger' or 'Warning') goes on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous; an unclassified mixture has none. A labelling duty, not a passport one. Reg. (EU) 2026/405 Annex VI Part A carries no CLP item; Part B lets the passport include the Art. 17 label information.

hazardPictograms.title: Hazard Pictograms
hazardPictograms.description: Array of GHS pictogram codes applicable to the product (GHS01 through GHS09).
hazardPictograms.x-citationNote: CLP Art. 19: hazard pictograms go on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous; none for an unclassified mixture. A labelling duty, not a passport one. Reg. (EU) 2026/405 Annex VI Part A carries no CLP item; Part B lets the passport include the Art. 17 label information.

hazardStatements.title: Hazard Statements
hazardStatements.description: Array of H-code hazard statements with full text.
hazardStatements.x-citationNote: CLP Art. 21: hazard statements (H-codes) go on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous; none for an unclassified mixture. A labelling duty, not a passport one. Reg. (EU) 2026/405 Annex VI Part A carries no CLP item; Part B lets the passport include the Art. 17 label information.

precautionaryStatements.title: Precautionary Statements
precautionaryStatements.description: Array of P-code precautionary statements with full text.
precautionaryStatements.x-citationNote: CLP Art. 22 puts precautionary statements on the LABEL of mixtures classified as hazardous. Not passport data under Annex VI Part A, and not owed for an unclassified product.

supplementalHazardInfo.title: Supplemental Hazard Information
supplementalHazardInfo.x-citationNote: CLP Annex II covers supplemental label information — EUH statements and similar. The obligation is to place that text ON THE LABEL; a passport copy repeats it rather than discharging it.

ufi.title: Unique Formula Identifier (UFI)
ufi.description: 16-character alphanumeric code linking the product to its poison centre notification. Required for hazardous mixtures.
ufi.x-citationNote: CLP Annex VIII Part A 3.1 and Art. 25(7): a UFI for mixtures classified for health or physical hazards and notified under Art. 45; not for mixtures classified only as gases under pressure or explosives (point 2.2). A labelling and notification duty, not a passport one. Reg. (EU) 2026/405 Annex VI Part A carries no CLP item; Part B lets the passport include the Art. 17 label information.

poisonCentreNotificationNumber.title: Poison Centre Notification Number
poisonCentreNotificationNumber.description: Notification number from ECHA poison centres notification portal.
poisonCentreNotificationNumber.x-citationNote: CLP Annex VIII governs notification of hazardous mixtures to the bodies appointed under Art. 45 for emergency health response. The duty is discharged by NOTIFYING those bodies — a database entry — and the resulting UFI belongs on the label. Publishing the notification reference in a passport neither creates nor satisfies the obligation.

emergencyPhoneNumber.title: Emergency Phone Number
emergencyPhoneNumber.description: 24-hour emergency telephone number for chemical incidents.
emergencyPhoneNumber.x-citationNote: Safety-data-sheet content (section 1.4). REACH Art. 31(1) requires a safety data sheet only for mixtures classified as dangerous (and certain PBT/vPvB or Candidate-List cases), and Art. 31(4) lets a product sold to the general public with sufficient information go without one. Not passport data under Annex VI Part A.

productCategoryEuPCS.title: EU Product Categorisation System (EuPCS)
productCategoryEuPCS.description: Product category code under the European Product Categorisation System for poison centre notifications.
productCategoryEuPCS.x-citationNote: The EuPCS category is part of the poison-centre notification under CLP Annex VIII, owed only for mixtures classified for health or physical hazards. It is a notification to appointed bodies, not passport data.

svhcSubstances.title: SVHC / Substances of Concern
svhcSubstances.description: Array of Substances of Very High Concern present above 0.1% w/w. REACH Art. 33 applies to articles, not mixtures; for detergents and paints the relevant duty is the safety data sheet (Art. 31(1)(c), 31(3)(b)). For detergents, Annex VI Part A(h) of Reg (EU) 2026/405 covers SVHCs in the passport. The passport is not compelled to carry this by REACH Art. 33.
svhcSubstances.x-citationNote: REACH Art. 33 applies to articles, not mixtures. For a detergent the SVHC duty is the safety data sheet (REACH Art. 31(1)(c), 31(3)(b)); the passport is not compelled to carry this list, and the Reg. (EU) 2026/405 Annex VI Part A(h) ingredient list covers SVHCs present.

svhcEcNumber.title: SVHC EC Number
svhcEcNumber.description: EC number for the SVHC substance.
svhcEcNumber.x-citationNote: REACH Art. 33 is the SVHC communication duty and it is narrower than it looks: to business recipients, and to consumers ON REQUEST within 45 days, for articles containing an SVHC above 0.1% w/w, with a minimum content of the substance NAME. Publishing an EC number proactively exceeds what any in-force provision requires.

svhcLocationInProduct.title: SVHC Location in Product
svhcLocationInProduct.description: Where in the product the SVHC substance is present.
svhcLocationInProduct.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

svhcCandidateListDate.title: SVHC Candidate List Date
svhcCandidateListDate.description: Date when the substance was added to the ECHA SVHC candidate list.
svhcCandidateListDate.x-citationNote: REACH Art. 59 governs how a substance is added to the candidate list. The date of inclusion determines when the Art. 33 communication and SCIP notification duties bite for that substance; it is a fact about the list rather than a datum the manufacturer is required to publish.

svhcScipNotificationId.title: SCIP Notification ID
svhcScipNotificationId.description: SCIP database notification identifier from ECHA for articles containing SVHCs.
svhcScipNotificationId.x-citationNote: The SCIP database notification is required by Waste Framework Directive Art. 9(1)(i), in force since 5 January 2021, for articles containing candidate-list substances above 0.1% w/w. The duty is discharged by notifying ECHA — a database entry — not by publishing the resulting identifier.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Physical appearance of the product (colour, form).
appearance.x-citationNote: Safety-data-sheet content (section 9.1). REACH Art. 31(1) requires a safety data sheet only for mixtures classified as dangerous (and certain PBT/vPvB or Candidate-List cases), and Art. 31(4) lets a product sold to the general public with sufficient information go without one.

ph.title: pH
ph.description: pH value of the product (as supplied or at specified dilution).
ph.x-citationNote: Safety-data-sheet content (section 9.1 in the current Annex II). REACH Art. 31(1) requires a safety data sheet only for mixtures classified as dangerous (and certain PBT/vPvB or Candidate-List cases), and Art. 31(4) lets a product sold to the general public with sufficient information go without one.

flashPoint.title: Flash Point
flashPoint.description: Flash point temperature of the product.

density.title: Density
density.description: Density or specific gravity of the product.

viscosity.title: Viscosity
viscosity.description: Dynamic or kinematic viscosity of the product.

carbonFootprint.title: Carbon Footprint
carbonFootprint.description: Product carbon footprint value in kg CO2 equivalent.

recyclability.description: Percentage recyclability of the product packaging.

endOfLifeInstructions.title: End-of-Life Instructions
endOfLifeInstructions.description: Instructions for proper disposal of the product and its packaging.
endOfLifeInstructions.x-citationNote: Safety-data-sheet content (section 13, disposal considerations). REACH Art. 31(1) requires a safety data sheet only for mixtures classified as dangerous (and certain PBT/vPvB or Candidate-List cases), and Art. 31(4) lets a product sold to the general public with sufficient information go without one.

dataCarrierType.title: Data Carrier Type
dataCarrierType.description: Type of data carrier used for the DPP (QR code, NFC, RFID, etc.).
dataCarrierType.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

dataCarrierUri.title: Data Carrier URI
dataCarrierUri.description: GS1 Digital Link URI encoded in the data carrier.
dataCarrierUri.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

passportValidFrom.title: Passport Valid From
passportValidFrom.description: Date from which the digital product passport is valid.
passportValidFrom.x-citationNote: ESPR Art. 10 governs the passport's TECHNICAL design — data carrier, unique identifiers, access rights, availability — not which product data must be published. The substantive obligation still arrives via an Art. 4 delegated act, and none is adopted for this category. Anticipated; voluntary today. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

passportRetentionYears.title: Passport Retention Period (Years)
passportRetentionYears.description: Number of years the DPP must be retained and accessible. Default is 10 years per ESPR.
passportRetentionYears.x-citationNote: ESPR Art. 10 governs the passport's TECHNICAL design — data carrier, unique identifiers, access rights, availability — not which product data must be published. The substantive obligation still arrives via an Art. 4 delegated act, and none is adopted for this category. Anticipated; voluntary today. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

accessLevel.title: Access Level
accessLevel.description: Default access level controlling who can view the passport data.
accessLevel.x-citationNote: ESPR Art. 10 governs the passport's TECHNICAL design — data carrier, unique identifiers, access rights, availability — not which product data must be published. The substantive obligation still arrives via an Art. 4 delegated act, and none is adopted for this category. Anticipated; voluntary today. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
ingredients.description: Array of ingredients/substances in the product, each with name, identifiers, concentration and function.
ingredients.x-citationNote: Annex VI Part A(h) requires the full list of intentionally added substances, each identified per CLP Art. 18(3) (name plus identification number where one exists), with no amounts. It does not apply to industrial and institutional detergents whose SDS carries the equivalent, and the template cannot yet express that condition, so the field is optional. Label bands (Annex V Part A 1(h)(i)) and functions may be recorded per entry but are label content, not Part A(h).

surfactantsTotal.title: Total Surfactants (%)
surfactantsTotal.description: Total weight percentage of all surfactants in the product.
surfactantsTotal.x-citationNote: Banded ingredient content is an Annex V Part A LABEL obligation. There is no concentration or percentage anywhere in Annex VI Part A, so a total-surfactant figure discharges the labelling duty, not the passport one.

phosphatesContent.title: Phosphates Content (% P2O5)
phosphatesContent.description: Total phosphorus content expressed as P2O5 percentage.
phosphatesContent.x-citationNote: A banded content figure under Annex V Part A, which is the LABEL. The Annex VI Part A passport dataset carries no amounts.

phosphonatesContent.title: Phosphonates Content (%)
phosphonatesContent.description: Total phosphonate content as weight percentage.
phosphonatesContent.x-citationNote: A banded content figure under Annex V Part A, which is the LABEL. The Annex VI Part A passport dataset carries no amounts.

edtaContent.title: EDTA Content
edtaContent.description: Content of EDTA and its salts (chelating agent) as weight percentage.
edtaContent.x-citationNote: A banded content figure under Annex V Part A, which is the LABEL. The Annex VI Part A passport dataset carries no amounts.

soapContent.title: Soap Content
soapContent.description: Weight percentage of soap (fatty acid salts) in the formulation.
soapContent.x-citationNote: A banded content figure under Annex V Part A, which is the LABEL. The Annex VI Part A passport dataset carries no amounts.

opticalBrighteners.title: Optical Brighteners Present
opticalBrighteners.description: Whether the product contains optical brighteners / fluorescent whitening agents.
opticalBrighteners.x-citationNote: Optical brightener disclosure is an Annex V Part A labelling item under Reg (EU) 2026/405, applying from 23 Sep 2029. It is not among the nine Annex VI Part A passport points.

enzymes.title: Enzymes
enzymes.description: Array of enzyme types used in the product (e.g. protease, lipase, amylase, cellulase).
enzymes.x-citationNote: Enzymes appear as an Annex V Part A labelling category. The passport's own duty is the Annex VI Part A point (h) list of intentionally added substances; a separate enzyme field is label-shaped, not passport-shaped.

microorganisms.title: Microorganisms
microorganisms.description: Array of microorganisms used in the product, with species and strain identifiers. Conditional — required only if product contains added microorganisms.
microorganisms.x-citationNote: Annex VI Part A(i) requires the list of intentionally added micro-organisms with genus, species and strain; a product with none has an empty list, so the field is optional.

ultimateBiodegradation.title: Ultimate Biodegradation
ultimateBiodegradation.description: Whether the surfactants in the product achieve ultimate aerobic biodegradation.
ultimateBiodegradation.x-citationNote: Surfactant biodegradability is a market-placement CONDITION — a surfactant must meet the ultimate-biodegradation criterion to be placed on the market, with the test evidence held in the technical documentation. Passing is the duty; publishing the result is not among the Annex VI Part A passport points.

biodegradationTestMethod.title: Biodegradation Test Method
biodegradationTestMethod.description: Test method used to show ultimate aerobic biodegradation under Reg. (EU) 2026/405 Annex I A.2: Reg. 440/2008 methods C.4-C/D/E/F (>=60% in 28 d) or C.4-A/B (>=70% in 28 d), i.e. the OECD 301 series. No pre-adaptation, no 10-day window.
biodegradationTestMethod.x-citationNote: The test method underpins the biodegradability evidence held in the technical documentation. It is not an Annex VI Part A passport point and not label content.

degradationPercent.title: Degradation Percentage
degradationPercent.description: Percentage of biodegradation achieved in the standard test.
degradationPercent.x-citationNote: The measured degradation figure is evidence supporting the biodegradability condition, held in the technical documentation rather than published. Annex VI Part A carries no percentages.

passThreshold.title: Pass Threshold Met
passThreshold.description: Whether the product meets the minimum biodegradation pass threshold (typically >=60%).
passThreshold.x-citationNote: The pass threshold is a property of the test criterion, not of the product. It is neither Annex V Part A label content nor an Annex VI Part A passport point.

recommendedDoseMl.title: Recommended Dose (mL)
recommendedDoseMl.description: Recommended dosage in millilitres for a standard use cycle.
recommendedDoseMl.x-citationNote: Dosage instructions are Annex V Part B LABEL content for consumer laundry detergents (point 1(a)); points 3 and 4 cover dishwasher and surface detergents. Annex VI Part A does not include dosage.

waterHardnessRange.title: Water Hardness Range
waterHardnessRange.description: Water hardness range for which the recommended dose applies (soft/medium/hard).
waterHardnessRange.x-citationNote: Water hardness is a reference condition for the Annex V Part A dosage statement on the LABEL, not an Annex VI Part A passport point.

machineLoadsPerPackage.title: Machine Loads per Package
machineLoadsPerPackage.description: Number of standard machine loads achievable from one package.
machineLoadsPerPackage.x-citationNote: The number of standard machine loads per package is an Annex V Part B LABEL statement for consumer laundry detergents (point 1(b)). It is not passport content under Annex VI Part A.

usageInstructionsText.title: Usage Instructions
usageInstructionsText.description: Detailed usage instructions for the product.
usageInstructionsText.x-citationNote: Annex V Part A 1(e) puts instructions for use on the LABEL, 'where necessary and relevant'. Annex VI Part B lets the passport carry label information, but Part A does not require it.

intendedUse.title: Intended Use
intendedUse.description: Description of the product's intended use and application scope.
intendedUse.x-citationNote: Safety-data-sheet content (section 1.2). REACH Art. 31(1) requires a safety data sheet only for mixtures classified as dangerous (and certain PBT/vPvB or Candidate-List cases), and Art. 31(4) lets a product sold to the general public with sufficient information go without one.

issuedUnderSoleResponsibility.title: Issued Under Manufacturer's Sole Responsibility
issuedUnderSoleResponsibility.description: The manufacturer's indication that this passport is issued under its sole responsibility (Reg (EU) 2026/405 Annex VI Part A(e); Art. 21(9)). A statement by the manufacturer: the platform pre-fills it when the manufacturer creates the passport, and creating the passport is the manufacturer's act, not the platform's.

complianceDemonstrated.title: Compliance Demonstrated
complianceDemonstrated.description: The manufacturer's statement that compliance of the detergent or end-user surfactant with Reg (EU) 2026/405 has been demonstrated (Annex VI Part A(g); Art. 21(2)(b)). Made by the manufacturer; the platform only records it. References to other Union law complied with belong in the EU declaration of conformity.
